missionPremise: The operator's requirement, carried in the dispatch in his words: Development services must match the data the PRODUCTION Bastrop dashboard displays today, because it monitors the MyGov system the city already runs. _inbox/2026-08-19_template_city_lens_build_sheet.md:84 lists MyGov across sixteen endpoints; the product modelled two of them, `permits` as `permits-pipeline` and `work-orders`. This lane adds the three that close the named gap. Underneath it sits RULING 1, operator-approved 2026-08-19 in the same build sheet: 'not built' moved down one level, from describing the SURFACE to describing SOURCES, because the product could not distinguish 'we did not build Parks' from 'your city has no Parks data' and those are different sentences to a customer. G-91 built the seam that makes the distinction expressible; this lane is one of the wave-2 lanes that fans onto it, and it was dispatched FIRST because Development services is the lens with a live production comparison.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this without me by running six things in the clone at P:/tmp/w2ds-dash on branch g92/dev-services-domains. (1) `node --test src/*.test.mjs` returns 294 pass, 0 fail, against a 273 pass baseline on the base SHA. (2) `GET /api/city-domains?cityKey=template-city` returns 7 regions of which `inspections`, `code-violations` and `business-licenses` read `ok` with 21, 19 and 17 records. (3) `GET /api/domains/<each>?cityKey=empty-city` returns `no-fixture-source` with a basis and zero records. (4) Composing the three twice in two SEPARATE node processes produces byte-identical output. (5) Neutering either content guard in src/fixture-seam.mjs turns the lane's rejection tests red, and restoring it turns them green. (6) `git diff --stat origin/main -- web/` is empty. All six are recorded below with raw results.
scopeBasis: IN, and why these boundaries. The three MyGov record types the build sheet names and nothing else from the sixteen endpoints: `permits/stats`, `work-orders/{daily-queue,geo-clusters,sla,stats}`, `reviews/summary` and `sync-status` are all aggregates or companions OF the two already-modelled domains, and `reviews/summary` belongs to Plan review, which the build sheet:125 rules is a separate lens and directional (Plan review aspirationally replaces what DS monitors). Each new domain gets its record shape, its second dimension, its extras, and its registry line. OUT and deliberately so: anything under `web/`, because a sibling lane owns it on this card and a collision there costs both lanes; any RENDERING of these three regions, for the same reason; the other wave-2 lenses, which are the sibling lane's card; connecting a feed or granting an adapter, which the standing decisions forbid and the dispatch places out of scope; the code-enforcement either/or the build sheet:114 flags (DS tab versus department home), which is an operator ruling and is left open by declaring the DATA once under one lensId so either ruling is a consumer change; merging and deploying, which are planner-owned. NOT out of scope but NOT DONE, stated so it is not mistaken for an exclusion: the three regions reach no pixel.
